content.data:
All three files are done. Here's a summary of everything built:

---

**Files created:**
- `index.html` — structure
- `style.css` — 611 lines of styling
- `app.js` — 392 lines of logic

**What's implemented:**

| Feature | Detail |
|---|---|
| 🕐 Clock | Live `hh:mm:ss` updating every second |
| 📅 Date | Full locale date string below clock |
| 👋 Greeting | "Good Morning/Afternoon/Evening/Night, [Name]" |
| 👤 Name modal | Shown on first visit, stored in `localStorage`, editable via "✏️ Change Name" |
| 🌙 Dark mode | Toggle button on top card, persists across refreshes |
| ⏱ Focus Timer | 25:00 countdown, Start/Stop/Reset, flashes when done |
| ✅ Tasks | Add/delete/check-off, duplicate detection (case-insensitive), persists |
| 🔗 Quick Links | Add named URL pills, delete with ×, pre-seeded with Google/Gmail/Calendar |
| 📱 Responsive | Single column on mobile, two-column middle row on desktop |

**To open:** Just double-click `index.html` in your file explorer — no server needed.

GitHub no longer accepts passwords for git operations. You need to use a **Personal Access Token (PAT)** instead. Here's how to fix it:

**Option 1 — Update your remote URL with a token:**
1. Go to GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Generate new token (classic)
2. Give it `repo` scope and copy the token
3. Run this in your terminal, replacing `YOUR_TOKEN` and `YOUR_USERNAME`:
```
git remote set-url origin https://YOUR_USERNAME:YOUR_TOKEN@github.com/myuyami/CodingCamp-05October26-nasywagadizatiarakhumaira.git
git push origin main
```

**Option 2 — Use GitHub CLI (easier):**
```
gh auth login
git push origin main
```

Once authenticated, the push will go through. The commit is already saved locally so nothing is lost.
